draftContext.markdown:
Native-dispatch probe redesign: no PR open, no owner assigned. Empty Codex allowlist is the correct state until a probe exists that tests tool fields in real ChatGPT-subscription rollouts. This is not a timed decay — the allowlist stays empty until the probe design is reviewed and passes. Owner assignment is an operator decision.

Core #594 merge status is ambiguous — listed in merged-7-day window but no in-window merge timestamp recorded. Needs a ten-second check against the PR before next publish.

Core #590 (NAS tenant identity ADR) has been open since 2026-11-08 with no recorded activity. Either it is blocked on a named dependency (candidate: #595 NAS migration plan) or it should be explicitly parked with a stated reason. An ADR held open this long without recorded movement is indistinguishable from abandoned.

Seven independent audit draft PRs (#533, #535, #537, #539, #541, #543, #545) have no defined merge criterion and no disposition process. The queue grows by one per published article. This needs a process decision before the next audit cycle, not another article entry.

BookcaseDiscovery 4K validation scope: ingest and test suite confirmed (1,905 passing, 13 skipped). Model inference against 4K tier not yet run. GPU measurement against sf-store-003 is the next card. OC35 (owner ruling on sf-store-005 held-out classification) is a governance gate independent of the technical measurement — sf-store-003 can be measured without resolving OC35.

macOS defaults preflight fix (PR #606): the two accepted message strings are pinned in the fix file. Any future macOS version introducing a new message variant will cause a preflight hold by design — that is the intended safe default. The file path where these strings are pinned should be referenced in the next debugging guide or onboarding doc for workstation-yuri.

Workstation-yuri #11 (Yojimbo device label) has no recorded CI event in this window. Status should be confirmed before merge eligibility is assumed.

The 30-minute same-device approval window in PR #605 is a session-scoped TTL on the supervised entry: the approval is bound to the originating device identity and expires after 30 minutes. This is a security boundary — anyone extending or modifying this window in future PRs should document the threat model change explicitly.
